_why: ADR 0191's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
ADR 0191 replaced first-match-wins with specificity scoring and widened
the keyword vocabulary from each domain's definition. The interesting
result was an ablation, not the headline: scoring alone moved the
independent set by zero points, and only became load-bearing once the
vocabulary was wide enough to create collisions for it to resolve.
S1 restores first-match-wins under the widened vocabulary -- the D arm
of that ablation. It is the mutation that shows scoring is doing work:
with the wide vocabulary in place, removing scoring costs accuracy on
the LLM-authored fixture.
The word-boundary matcher that S2 used to target is gone. The mutation
harness reported it NOT CAUGHT, which sent me to measure it rather than
to write a test for it: across all 131 labelled queries it changed no
classification at all. It was removed instead of tested. A mutation that
cannot be caught because the code does nothing is a signal about the code,
not a gap in the suite.
S3 restores the fallback-reported-as-a-match collapse, which ADR 0190
fixed and which this record's held-out reasoning depends on: if a
fallback cannot be seen, the fallback count that exposed the shared-
author bias cannot be seen either.
Not included, because these tests do not catch it: whether the labels in
the LLM-authored fixture are correct. They are the domain each query was
commissioned for, never independently verified, and no mutation here
tests that assumption. The ADR says so; a set file implying coverage
would overstate the evidence.
Run:  python3 scripts/mutate.py --set docs/mutations/adr-0191-classifier-scoring.json
test: cd Science-Agent-Pipeline/artifacts/api-server && npx vitest run src/__tests__/classifierEval.test.ts src/__tests__/llmAuthoredQueries.test.ts src/__tests__/llmConfigState.test.ts

mutations.description: specificity scoring reverts to first-match-wins over the table
mutations._claimed: caught by the fixed-defect tests and by the beats-what-it-replaced floor
mutations._note: The D arm of the ablation, as a mutation. Accuracy on the LLM-authored fixture falls from 62/78 to 59/78, and the repressilator and two-locus confusions triple -- the collisions the wider vocabulary introduced, which only scoring resolves. Every query still gets a domain, so nothing errors; the classifier just quietly gets worse.

mutations.description: the fallback reports itself as a genuine match again
mutations._claimed: caught by the three-state tests and the fallback bound
mutations._note: ADR 0190's defect, restored. The domain returned is unchanged, so every test asserting only on the domain still passes. This is the mutation that would let a future shared-author fixture look independent: with no visible fallback count, 'matched nothing' and 'answered mm' are one fact again.
